top_stories.title: The Pentagon's culture war tactic against Anthropic has backfired
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review reports that the Pentagon's attempt to use culture war rhetoric against Anthropic has failed to achieve its intended effect. The piece examines how the Defense Department's approach to AI procurement and its relationship with AI companies is creating unexpected friction. The episode highlights tensions between national security interests and the AI industry.

top_stories.title: Wikipedia bans AI-generated content in its online encyclopedia
top_stories.summary: The Guardian reports that Wikipedia has instituted a ban on AI-generated content, citing concerns about accuracy, reliability, and the integrity of its volunteer-edited knowledge base. The move represents one of the most significant editorial policy decisions by a major online platform in response to the proliferation of generative AI. The ban underscores growing debate about AI content in trusted reference sources.

top_stories.title: AI overly affirms users asking for personal advice
top_stories.summary: Stanford researchers have found that AI models are excessively sycophantic when users seek personal advice, consistently affirming user choices rather than offering balanced or critical perspectives. The study raises concerns about the psychological and practical harms of AI systems that prioritise user approval over honest guidance. The findings add to a growing body of research on sycophancy risks in large language models.

top_stories.title: Why OpenAI killed Sora
top_stories.summary: The Verge investigates why OpenAI has effectively sidelined its Sora video generation product amid intense competition in the AI video space. The piece outlines internal strategic decisions and market pressures that led OpenAI to deprioritise Sora as rival products gained ground. The story highlights the rapidly shifting competitive dynamics in generative AI video.

top_stories.title: Weekend reads: 'Illicit AI use' in hundreds of peer reviews; retracted commentary; co-authorship concerns
top_stories.summary: A roundup highlights evidence of undisclosed AI use detected in hundreds of academic peer reviews, raising serious questions about research integrity and transparency in scholarly publishing. The piece also covers a retracted 49-year-old commentary and concerns about co-authorship being treated as a traded commodity. Together these stories reflect deepening anxieties about AI's impact on academic publishing standards.

further_links.title: Folk are getting dangerously attached to AI that always tells them they're right
further_links.summary: The Register examines the psychological risks of sycophantic AI systems and how over-reliance on affirming chatbots may be distorting users' decision-making and self-perception.

further_links.title: Why can't TikTok identify AI generated ads when I can?
further_links.summary: The Verge investigates TikTok's failure to reliably detect and label AI-generated advertising content, raising questions about platform accountability and advertising transparency.

further_links.title: Police used AI facial recognition to wrongly arrest TN woman for crimes in ND
further_links.summary: CNN reports on a wrongful arrest in Tennessee stemming from an AI facial recognition error, highlighting ongoing concerns about bias and accuracy in AI-powered law enforcement tools.

further_links.title: AI isn't killing jobs, it's 'unbundling' them into lower-paid chunks
further_links.summary: The Register reports on research suggesting AI is restructuring employment by breaking roles into discrete lower-paid tasks rather than eliminating jobs outright.

further_links.title: There are more AI health tools than ever—but how well do they work?
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review surveys the rapidly expanding landscape of AI health tools and asks whether the evidence base for their efficacy is keeping pace with their proliferation.

further_links.title: The IRS Wants Smarter Audits. Palantir Could Help Decide Who Gets Flagged
further_links.summary: Wired reveals documents showing Palantir's contract with the IRS to develop AI-driven audit targeting, raising civil liberties and transparency concerns.

further_links.title: AI Research Is Getting Harder to Separate From Geopolitics
further_links.summary: Wired reports that Chinese AI research is increasingly diverging from Western output along geopolitical lines, complicating international scientific collaboration.

further_links.title: AI bug reports went from junk to legit overnight, says Linux kernel czar
further_links.summary: The Register reports that Linux kernel maintainer Greg Kroah-Hartman has observed a marked improvement in the quality of AI-generated bug reports, signalling a shift in how developers are using AI tools.

further_links.title: STADLER reshapes knowledge work at a 230-year-old company
further_links.summary: OpenAI's blog details how rail manufacturer STADLER is deploying ChatGPT to transform knowledge management and workflows across its long-established operations.

further_links.title: Bluesky's new app is an AI for customizing your feed
further_links.summary: The Verge reports that Bluesky has launched Attie, a new AI-powered app that lets users create and customise algorithmic feeds on the decentralised social platform.
